name: EIA/TIA-232 family and the PC serial-port implementation

era.notes: This reading slice compares V.24 (02/2000) definitions with the IBM PC April 1984 documented implementation; these source dates are not interface lifecycle dates.

physical.notes: Documented object boundaries only; full standard/implementation contact mapping remains gated.

electrical.notes: IBM implementation and UART/line-interface boundary only; no complete electrical-standard or device-safety review.

signaling.notes: Data/control and UART framing are distinguished; full timing/framing/version comparison is unfinished.

protocol.notes: Limited to selected DTE/DCE data/control circuit definitions in V.24 (02/2000), not a complete communications protocol.

host.notes: Limited to the IBM April 1984 Technical Reference BIOS/8250 services and send/status reading path; no modern OS or adapter claims.

ecosystem.notes: IBM external-modem context and later TI PC application context only; lifecycle and replacement/continuity research is unfinished.

evidence_summary.notes: Two E1 sources (V.24 and IBM publication 6361453) and one E2 TI application note were used. No E3 emulation or E4 measurement was performed.

safety_notes: No executable pin-to-pin, null-modem, hot-plug, or TTL-UART-to-RS-232 wiring instructions are provided.
TIA/ISO full-text and edition review, specific endpoint and cable evidence, electrical levels, directions, grounding, power, and hot-plug conditions remain unresolved.
open_questions: Obtain and review the official TIA entry/full text, relevant ISO 2110 editions, IBM 9-contact original documentation, and edition differences identified in the source map.
Complete lifecycle, use-case-specific replacement and inheritance research before asserting relationship records.
Establish sources for any selected modern OS, driver, adapter, and reproducible experiment before describing their behavior.
